title: To fulfill all righteousness (Matthew 3:13–17)
hookLine: John protests; Jesus insists on being baptized like everyone else
tomorrow: how do you answer a voice that quotes the Bible back?

cards: Shoes off, belt off, everyone shuffling forward at airport security, the executive and the college kid holding the same gray bin. A line makes everyone the same height.

There's a line at the Jordan too: people waiting their turn to go under with John, confessing their sins. And Matthew says: "Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him." Not to watch.

teach.b: John sees who it is and tries to stop him: "I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?" Fair question. Why would the mightier one ask for a washing meant for people confessing their sins?

teach.h: SUFFER IT TO BE SO NOW.
teach.b: Jesus answers: "Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness." Suffer means let. Righteousness here is doing what's right in God's eyes, all of it, nothing skipped.
So feel the scene: the same muddy bank, the same cold river, the same wet hair as the person ahead of him. Matthew doesn't say more about why, and Christians read it more than one way.
Some hear him standing with sinners, shoulder to shoulder with the whole human crowd. Some hear an example for everyone baptized after him. Some hear plain obedience.
Then, coming up out of the water, he sees "the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him," and a voice says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
One to tell a friend tonight: in Matthew the voice comes before Jesus has preached a sermon or healed anyone.
What he has done is stand in line.

how: Some churches keep a feast of the Baptism of the Lord, and Orthodox churches remember Jesus' baptism at Theophany, often with a blessing of water.

games.q: what does “to fulfill all righteousness” mean?
o: doing all God asks, even waiting in line
keeping a record of every law you've kept
being more perfect than anyone around you

games.q: to fulfill all righteousness — tap the pairs.
p: I have need to be baptized of thee
suffer it to be so now

s: John agreed at once to baptize Jesus
John forbad him: I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?
in Matthew, the voice from heaven comes before Jesus has preached or healed
it comes at his baptism, as he comes up out of the water.
Jesus was baptized apart, after the crowd had gone
Matthew gives no private ceremony; he comes to John like the others, to be baptized of him.

games.q: at a packed clinic, the receptionist recognizes you and offers to slip you ahead of the whole waiting room. what fits today's story?
o: thank her, and wait your turn with everyone else.
take the spot; a little favor now and then is fine.
wait, but mention to people that you could've skipped.
games.why: Jesus could have been the exception. he asked for the same water as everyone else: suffer it to be so now.

practice: Stand up, if you can, feet planted and hands loose at your sides, the way people stand in a line.
Let the strangers you'll wait beside this week come to mind, at a register, a bus stop, a clinic, and stay right there with them: not ahead, not apart, one more person waiting.

wordCard.voice: To fulfill all righteousness. Jesus' answer to John: let it be so, in the same river as everyone else.

orig.note: Greek: righteousness, also justice. the word behind righteousness in Matthew 3:15.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: in line with sinners, which is where the voice from heaven found him. Go well.
